result.title: The Bayesian Learning Rule Beyond KL Geometry
result.summary: The Bayesian learning rule (BLR) exploits the relation between Bayesian updating and the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) to derive efficient additive updates for exponential family variational posteriors. The KL geometry is powerful but restrictive: combined with posterior families with parameter-dependent support it can lead to undefined objectives. We ask which non-KL geometries preserve the additive BLR computation. Previous works that use $f$-divergences suggest that this is only possible with the KLD. Here, we show that this is not true. We show that additive information-geometric optimization algorithms can be derived for the class of mixed-space Bregman or Fenchel-Young discrepancies. These discrepancies induce generalized maximum-entropy families, dual coordinates, and generalized-BLR canonical gradient updates, recovering the classical BLR. The generalized BLR leads to new algorithms that \textit{cannot} be derived from the KL-based BLR. For the Tsallis negentropy with quadratic statistics, the generalized BLR yields bounded-support and heavy-tailed $q$-Gaussian posteriors and an easy Newton-like implementation. Experiments up to CIFAR-100 illustrate controllable support and tail behavior and competitive performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文追问 KL 几何之外哪些非 KL 散度仍能保持 Bayesian learning rule 的可加更新，证明 mixed-space Bregman 或 Fenchel–Young 差异可导出广义最大熵族、对偶坐标与广义 BLR，并给出 q-Gaussian 后验的 Newton 式实现及 CIFAR-100 实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对偶坐标下的加性状态更新与「表示几何」问题可能为 latent 推理状态的更新规则设计提供概念线索，但原文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，是否适用于序列潜变量推断有待核查。
